headline: 5 killed as fire guts Cox's Bazar resort
summary: A blaze destroyed the TUPTUP Resto and Resort at Inani Beach, with authorities fearing several casualties.
details: A massive fire ripped through the TUPTUP Resto and Resort at Cox's Bazar's Inani Beach on Saturday morning. Authorities suspect that around five people may have died in the blaze.
The fire broke out around 6:30 am near Patuartek Beach along Marine Drive. The resort, which was built largely of bamboo and wood, was completely destroyed by the flames.
Syed Muhammad Morshed Hossain, deputy assistant director of the Cox's Bazar Fire Service, stated that all three floors of the wooden structure had burnt down.
Police and Fire Service teams worked at the scene to search for victims. The cause of the fire and the full extent of the damage were not immediately clear.
The resort is located approximately 29km from Kolatoli at the entrance to the beach town.

headline_marked: 335 lives lost: [[PM Tarique Rahman visits hospitals]] to assess dengue situation
headline: 335 lives lost: PM Tarique Rahman visits hospitals to assess dengue situation
summary: The Prime Minister inspected prevention measures and cleanliness at various healthcare and educational institutions across Dhaka amid a severe outbreak.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited several hospitals and educational institutions across Dhaka on Saturday to inspect dengue prevention measures and overall cleanliness.
His itinerary included the Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital in Uttara, Dhaka Medical College Hospital, and other facilities within the Dhaka North and South city corporation areas.
The visits are part of a broader effort following a three-month dengue prevention campaign launched by the Prime Minister on September 12, which focuses on public awareness and cleanliness.
According to the latest figures from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the dengue outbreak has claimed 335 lives this year.
The crisis has seen 108,440 total hospitalisations this year, with September being the deadliest month, recording 148 deaths and 43,774 admissions.
October has already seen 90 deaths, while Friday alone reported four more deaths and 1,181 new hospital admissions.
